items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Who did Bob have in his band there while we were?

ctx.x: And he come along though, he come along because I'll tell ya, who was it?

Some man got up and started singing the blues, a trumpet player, I don't know who you were now, in Bob Lyons band, he played trumpet and he sung the blues and after that where everybody's trumpet player started singing. Who could that been anyhow? Let me see what Bob used to have with him. Boy used to write music, what did he name, not Mad Cat, he used to play with him. You know this boy, he ain't been dead long. He used to play with him. Lewis, what was his name, Lewis? Lewis Dumaine. Lewis Dumaine. He sang the…
Well what did the Dots boys play?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Well, Chester Zottis, George Foster, and Bob Lyons.

ctx.x: He left kind of early too. Who were some of the good bass players down here? Huh? Who were some of the good bass players that played with writing bands?

Uh, bass violins? Uh huh. Chester Boone? Uh huh. Chester Boone? You know him? Chester who? No, Chester Zottis. Yeah. They got a Chester Boone in Houston. Now he's a player, that's all his name, Chester Boone. Well, Chester Zottis, George Foster, and Bob Lyons. Johnny, uh, used to play trombone and got on bass at the day. Was it Johnny?
Who did he play with? He played the Rover Show, yeah.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1971-04-08
items.q: the first people I saw was playing at the 25, Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots, and Bob Lyons on bass

ctx.x: since you're both sick right now.

Well, about me and Louis, I'll tell you about that. Uh... I left the country in 1918, and I was 18 years old. I went to World War I, and when I came back, the first people I saw was playing at the 25, Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots, and Bob Lyons on bass, and Lorenzo Starrs on guitar, so... You had to play in a drum?
